prompt.context_jp: 早朝のル･ソベール＿、まだ客の気配もなく静まり返っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 早朝のル･ソベール＿、まだ客の気配もなく静まり返っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The scene opens on the shop in the early morning. Choose the particle that frames it as the topic the sentence will describe.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence sets Le Sober as the scene the narrator is about to describe — a classic topic use of は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would announce Le Sober as new/identifying information, as if answering 'which place is quiet?' That is not what this opening line is doing — it is painting the setting.

contrast_examples.en: (As for) the shop, it's quiet. — describing the shop
The SHOP is quiet. — identifying which place is quiet

prompt.context_jp: 厨房の裏口にひとり立つハナの息＿白く、指先は緊張で強ばっている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 厨房の裏口にひとり立つハナの息＿白く、指先は緊張で強ばっている。
prompt.prompt_en: The narrator shifts focus to Hana's breath, then her fingertips. Which particle fits the parallel topic frame?

feedback.correct_en: The second clause clearly uses 指先は — a parallel topic structure. ハナの息は matches it: 'as for her breath... as for her fingertips...'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the breath newly spotted information, breaking the parallel with 指先は that follows.

contrast_examples.jp: 息は白く、指先は強ばっている。
contrast_examples.en: Her breath is white; her fingertips are stiff. (parallel topics)
Her breath is white! (noticing it for the first time)

prompt.context_jp: 窓の外は薄曇りで、株価表示のモニターだけ＿忙しく数字を更新している。
prompt.prompt_jp: 株価表示のモニターだけ＿忙しく数字を更新している。
prompt.prompt_en: Only the stock-price monitor is active in the still room. Which particle fits 'X alone is doing Y'?

feedback.correct_en: だけ+が singles the monitor out as the sole thing in motion — an exhaustive-listing use of が. The sentence identifies which thing, among all in the room, is active.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would shift to contrast ('the monitor, at least, …'), implying other things might also apply. The scene wants exclusive identification, not contrast with other items.

contrast_examples.en: Only he knows. (exhaustive)
He alone doesn't know. (contrastive)

prompt.context_jp: 壮亮の手にはル･ソベールの資料と、まだ誰にも見せていない出場計画＿握られていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 出場計画＿握られていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The narration reveals what Sōsuke is holding. Which particle introduces this new, identifying item?

feedback.correct_en: The clause reveals the existence of specific items in his hand — new information about what is there. Existential/discovery clauses with 〜が握られていた take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 出場計画 as an already-established topic, but the plan is being introduced to the reader for the first time here.

contrast_examples.jp: 机の上に手紙が置かれていた。
contrast_examples.en: A letter lay on the desk. (revealing what's there)

contrast_examples.jp: 手紙は机の上に置かれていた。
contrast_examples.en: The letter (we already know about) was on the desk.

prompt.context_jp: 厨房の隅で、ハナ＿何度も呼吸を整えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 厨房の隅で、ハナ＿何度も呼吸を整えた。
prompt.prompt_en: The narration returns to Hana as the paragraph's subject. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Hana is the ongoing protagonist whose actions the paragraph will describe — a classic topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would frame her as newly identified ('it was Hana who…'), but she is not new here; the narrator is continuing with her.

contrast_examples.en: She took a deep breath. (continuing with her)
SHE (of all people) took a deep breath. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: その夜、事務所に残った航＿ル･ソベールの通信履歴を睨みつけていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 事務所に残った航＿ル･ソベールの通信履歴を睨みつけていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The scene shifts to Kō, who now becomes the paragraph's topic. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: After a scene-setting phrase (その夜…), the narrator installs Kō as the new paragraph topic with は and then describes what he does.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'it is Kō who stayed and glared,' identifying him against alternatives — but the narration is simply following him, not contrasting him with others.

contrast_examples.jp: その夜、彼は書類を読んでいた。
contrast_examples.en: That night, he was reading documents. (topic)

contrast_examples.jp: その夜、彼が書類を読んでいた。
contrast_examples.en: That night, HE was reading the documents. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: ハナのノートパソコン＿一度もサイトに接続していなかったという事実は…
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナのノートパソコン＿一度もサイトに接続していなかったという事実…
prompt.prompt_en: Inside a 〜という事実 ('the fact that…') clause, which particle marks the subject?

feedback.correct_en: Subordinate clauses (relative/noun-complement) normally keep が for the internal subject; は is reserved for the matter-level topic (which comes right after: 事実は).
feedback.incorrect_en: Using は here would try to make ハナのノートパソコン the main topic — but 事実 is the main topic and takes its own は further on in the sentence.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来たという事実は重い。
contrast_examples.en: The fact that he came is weighty.
Awkward: two は's competing for topic.

prompt.context_jp: 「新入り＿天才ショコラティエ？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 新入り＿天才ショコラティエ？
prompt.prompt_en: The staff react in disbelief: 'The newbie — THE genius chocolatier?' Which particle fits an incredulous identification?

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is identifying who, out of everyone, is the genius — exhaustive/identificational が, with the sense 'she, of all people, is the one?'
feedback.incorrect_en: 新入りは would set 'the newbie' as a background topic and ask a neutral yes/no question about her, losing the shocked 'it's HER?!' nuance.

contrast_examples.en: HE's the culprit?! (identifying)
Is he a culprit? (neutral)

prompt.context_jp: ハナ＿飛び出していった通用口の先には、まだ朝の光が残っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナ＿飛び出していった通用口…
prompt.prompt_en: Inside a relative clause modifying 通用口, which particle marks the subject?

feedback.correct_en: Relative clauses almost always take が (or の) for their internal subject, because は is for the whole sentence's topic — which here is 通用口の先 marked by には.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a relative clause would try to set a topic that cannot escape the clause boundary — ungrammatical in this frame.

contrast_examples.en: The house he lives in is old.
Ungrammatical: competing topics.

prompt.context_jp: がらんとした部屋で、ハナ＿膝を抱えたまま長い時間動けずにいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナ＿膝を抱えたまま長い時間動けずにいた。
prompt.prompt_en: The scene reopens on Hana alone in a bare room. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: After the scene-setting phrase, the narrator installs Hana as the paragraph's topic and continues describing her state — topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as identifying her out of alternatives, which does not fit this quiet, continuing scene with Hana already in focus.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋で彼女は泣いていた。
contrast_examples.en: In the room she was crying. (topic)

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋で彼女が泣いていた。
contrast_examples.en: In the room, SHE was the one crying. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 壮亮の言葉＿耳の奥で何度も繰り返される。
prompt.prompt_jp: 壮亮の言葉＿耳の奥で何度も繰り返される。
prompt.prompt_en: Something unbidden intrudes on Hana. Which particle fits a spontaneous, perception-style event?

feedback.correct_en: Spontaneous/perceptual clauses — things echoing, appearing, being heard — introduce their subject with が, matching the way the words involuntarily surface in her mind.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'Sōsuke's words' an already-established topic, flattening the sudden, intrusive feeling the narration wants.

contrast_examples.en: A voice is heard. (sensation)
The voice (we're talking about) is audible. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: 時間だけ＿、彼女を置いてけぼりにして進んでいくようだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時間だけ＿、彼女を置いてけぼりにして進んでいく…
prompt.prompt_en: Only time keeps moving while she stays frozen. Which particle expresses 'X alone, uniquely'?

feedback.correct_en: だけ+が exhaustively identifies time as the sole thing moving — the right fit for 'nothing else, only time.'
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would be contrastive ('time, at least…'), implying other things might also apply — but the line insists on exclusivity.

contrast_examples.en: Only I remained. (exhaustive)
I alone stayed (as for me). (contrastive)

prompt.context_jp: 窓の外の街の音＿、この部屋には届かなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 窓の外の街の音＿、この部屋には届かなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: The city noise exists outside but does not reach the room. Which particle fits an implicit contrast ('outside yes, in here no')?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence sets up an implicit contrast — the sounds exist, but as for them (in this room), they didn't reach her. Contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the sounds as new information not reaching her, missing the pointed 'outside yes, inside no' contrast carried by は.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨の音は、部屋には届かない。
contrast_examples.en: The rain's sound (though out there) doesn't reach the room.
I hear rain. (new perception)

prompt.context_jp: 丁寧に整えられた文字の並びには、直接顔を合わせられないハナの声＿、そのまま乗っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナの声＿、そのまま乗っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Something newly 'rides' on the lines of the letter. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The scene reveals what is carried on the letter — Hana's voice. Discovery/existential 'X is there' takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark ハナの声 as an already-known topic, missing the quiet revelation the sentence stages.

contrast_examples.jp: 紙に思いが乗っている。
contrast_examples.en: Her feelings ride on the paper. (revealing)

contrast_examples.jp: 紙には思いは乗っていない。
contrast_examples.en: On the paper, those feelings aren't carried. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 「だって ハナさん＿好きなの壮亮じゃん」
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナさん＿好きなの壮亮じゃん。
prompt.prompt_en: Kō points out that, of all people, it is Sōsuke whom Hana likes. Which particle marks Hana as the one doing the liking inside this relative clause?

feedback.correct_en: ハナさんが好きなの (= the person Hana likes) is a relative clause; its internal subject takes が. The main clause's identification (壮亮じゃん) sits outside it.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this noun-modifying clause would try to make Hana the main topic, which conflicts with the cleft 〜のは〜 structure the speaker is using.

contrast_examples.jp: ハナさんが好きな人は壮亮だ。
contrast_examples.en: The person Hana likes is Sōsuke.

contrast_examples.jp: ハナさんは壮亮が好きだ。
contrast_examples.en: As for Hana, she likes Sōsuke. (different frame)

prompt.context_jp: 彼女にとって今回の大会＿単なる名誉ではない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 今回の大会＿単なる名誉ではない。
prompt.prompt_en: The narrator steps back to characterize what this contest means to her. Which particle fits for a general characterization/topic statement?

feedback.correct_en: 'As for this contest, it isn't merely about honor' — は frames the tournament and comments on its nature. Characterization statements take は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as identifying which contest isn't just honor, out of alternatives — not what the narration is doing.

contrast_examples.en: This match is special. (characterization)
THIS match (not others) is special. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: そう思わせるもの＿、彼を走らせていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: そう思わせるもの＿、彼を走らせていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The narrator asks what, precisely, is making him run. Which particle identifies 'it is X that…'?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence identifies the cause — it is that unnamed something that was driving him. Identificational が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the phrase into a mere topic ('as for the thing that made him think so…'), losing the pointed 'it was this that…' flavor.

contrast_examples.jp: ある思いが彼を動かした。
contrast_examples.en: A certain thought moved him. (identifying)

contrast_examples.jp: その思いは彼を動かした。
contrast_examples.en: That thought, (yes,) it moved him. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: その日の午後、双子製菓本社の一室＿、壮亮は父と机ひとつを挟んで向き合っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 双子製菓本社の一室＿、壮亮は父と向き合っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the room as the place where the action occurs?

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where an action (向き合っていた) takes place.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a point of existence or arrival (e.g. いる/行く), not the setting of an action. を would mark a direct object or path.

contrast_examples.en: Talk in the room. (action location)
Be in the room. (existence)

prompt.context_jp: 「ル･ソベールに もう一度 ＿＿＿ をください お願いします」
prompt.prompt_jp: もう一度＿＿＿をください。
prompt.prompt_en: Sōsuke pleads with his father to give Le Sober another ___. Pick the collocation.

feedback.correct_en: もう一度チャンスをください ('please give me another chance') is the natural set phrase for begging for another try.
feedback.incorrect_en: 機械 ('machine') is a homophone trap for 機会; 権利 ('right') and 命令 ('order') don't collocate with ください in this plea.

contrast_examples.en: Please give me a chance.

contrast_examples.jp: 機会を与えてください。
contrast_examples.en: Please give me an opportunity. (more formal)

prompt.context_jp: 「知らない人のサポートを するつもりは ＿＿＿ありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 知らない人のサポートをするつもりは＿＿＿ありません。
prompt.prompt_en: The staff flatly refuse to back a stranger. Pick the intensifier for a complete denial.

feedback.correct_en: 一切 + negative = 'not at all / absolutely not.' It's the natural collocation for a blanket refusal.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一応 ('for now/just in case'), 一旦 ('once/for the moment'), and 一見 ('at first glance') don't produce a complete denial here.

contrast_examples.en: I will not cooperate at all.
I'll cooperate, more or less.

prompt.prompt_en: The chief, admitting she needs the Anonymous Chocolatier's help, mutters this self-deprecating word.

feedback.correct_en: 情けない captures the pathetic/pitiful self-reproach of a chef who has to lean on a stranger.
feedback.incorrect_en: もったいない ('wasteful'), うらやましい ('enviable'), and とんでもない ('outrageous') don't fit this self-pity.

contrast_examples.en: I feel pathetic/ashamed of myself.
That's a waste.

prompt.context_jp: プライドを胸の奥に＿＿＿、彼女はもう一度社長室の扉を叩いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: プライドを胸の奥に＿＿＿、…扉を叩いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Motomi tucks her pride away before knocking again. Pick the verb for 'put away deep inside.'

feedback.correct_en: 胸の奥にしまう ('to tuck away in one's heart') is a set collocation for setting aside pride/feelings without abandoning them.
feedback.incorrect_en: 捨てる would mean she threw her pride away entirely — stronger than the scene suggests. 隠す ('hide') lacks the 'set aside until later' nuance. 預ける doesn't collocate with 胸の奥 this way.

contrast_examples.jp: 気持ちを胸の奥にしまう。
contrast_examples.en: To tuck one's feelings deep inside.
To throw away one's pride entirely.

prompt.context_jp: 「寛さんの片思いの相手に ＿＿＿を出して伝えるんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: ＿＿＿を出して伝えるんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Kiyomi urges Hiroshi to summon ___ and tell his crush how he feels.

feedback.correct_en: 勇気を出す ('to summon courage') is the fixed collocation for pushing yourself to do something scary — exactly what she's urging.
feedback.incorrect_en: 元気を出す is 'cheer up,' 本気を出す is 'get serious,' やる気を出す is 'get motivated' — none captures the fear of confessing feelings.

contrast_examples.jp: 勇気を出して告白した。
contrast_examples.en: I gathered my courage and confessed.
Cheer up!

prompt.context_jp: 「＿＿＿いかないっすわ 俺」
prompt.prompt_jp: ＿＿＿いかないっすわ、俺。
prompt.prompt_en: Kō vents, 'I can't ___ with this.' Pick the noun for 'acceptance / being convinced.'

feedback.correct_en: 納得がいかない ('can't accept / don't buy it') is the stock expression for refusing to be convinced.
feedback.incorrect_en: 我慢がいかない is not a phrase; 想像がいかない/理解がいかない aren't standard set collocations — the fixed form is 納得がいく/いかない.

contrast_examples.en: I can't accept it. (standard)
I can't understand. (uses できる, not いく)

prompt.context_jp: 「プライドは＿＿＿が、私のプライドなんかより…」
prompt.prompt_jp: プライドは＿＿＿ます。
prompt.prompt_en: Motomi admits her pride takes a hit. Pick the verb that collocates with プライド.

feedback.correct_en: プライドが傷つく ('one's pride is hurt') is the standard collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心が折れる exists ('heart breaks'), but プライドが折れる is not idiomatic. 壊れる/破れる don't pair with プライド in this way.

contrast_examples.en: One's pride is hurt.
One's spirit breaks.

prompt.context_jp: Kō charges in, having overheard the plan, to back the chief. Which line sounds most natural for his energetic, informal protest?
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Kō bursting in?

choices.text: チーフ 聞きましたよ いや チーフが 出るべきだと思います
チーフ 聞きました いや チーフは 出るべきだと思います
チーフ 聞いていました いや チーフこそ 出なくてはならないと存じます

feedback.correct_en: The original uses よ for the news-sharing push and チーフが to identify who, specifically, should enter. The flow matches Kō's agitated, kouhai register.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) drops よ and uses topic は, flattening the identification and the urgency. (c) over-formalizes with 存じます, which doesn't match Kō's casual kitchen voice.

contrast_examples.jp: チーフが出るべきです。
contrast_examples.en: Chief, YOU should enter. (identifying)

contrast_examples.jp: チーフは出るべきです。
contrast_examples.en: As for Chief, she should enter. (neutral topic)

prompt.context_jp: Handing off hot chocolate to a colleague, which short warning sounds most natural in the kitchen?
prompt.prompt_en: Which casual warning fits a working kitchen handoff?

choices.text: ちょっと熱いから気をつけて
少し熱いので注意してください
若干の熱がございますのでご留意ください

feedback.correct_en: Short, から-based casual warnings between kitchen colleagues sound natural and quick — matching the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is correct but overly polite for a quick handoff among coworkers. (c) is absurdly formal/business, out of place in a kitchen.

contrast_examples.en: Careful, it's hot. (casual)

contrast_examples.jp: お熱いのでご注意ください。
contrast_examples.en: Please be careful; it's hot. (customer-service register)

prompt.context_jp: Sōsuke presses Hana for why she stayed silent. Which phrasing sounds most natural for his pointed, hurt follow-up?
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits the hurt, pointed follow-up question?

choices.text: じゃあ なんで 言ってくれなかったんです？
じゃあ なんで 言わなかったですか？
では どうして 言わないんですか？

feedback.correct_en: 〜てくれなかった captures the emotional complaint 'you didn't do (me the favor of) telling'. んです adds the reaching-for-reason feel. なんで is the natural colloquial 'why.'
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) 言わなかったですか is grammatically awkward (〜なかったですか is marginal; 言いませんでしたか is standard) and loses 〜てくれる's emotional charge. (c) uses present tense, which doesn't fit a past silence.

contrast_examples.en: You didn't tell me. (with felt grievance)
(He) didn't tell. (neutral)

prompt.context_jp: In her letter, Hana apologizes for the deception. Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'I didn't want to deceive you'?
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits her written apology?

choices.text: だましたかったわけではありません
だましたかったことがありません
だまさなかったわけです

feedback.correct_en: 〜わけではない softens and precisifies: 'it isn't that I wanted to deceive you' — exactly the clarification her letter is making.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) 〜たことがありません means 'I have never done X,' which doesn't fit a want. (c) says 'I didn't deceive, that's the reason' — illogical given the context.

contrast_examples.en: It's not that I dislike it.
(ungrammatical/strange for this meaning)

prompt.context_jp: Kō gently tells Hana that her eyes are always searching for Sōsuke. Which phrasing sounds most natural?
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is most natural?

choices.text: ハナさんの目って ずっと壮亮を 探してるじゃないですか
ハナさんの目は ずっと壮亮が 探してるじゃないですか
ハナさんの目で ずっと壮亮を 探しているでしょう

feedback.correct_en: 〜って topicalizes casually, 壮亮を is the direct object of 探す, and 〜じゃないですか invites agreement — all natural for Kō's gentle observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) uses が for 壮亮, which would make Sōsuke the subject doing the searching — reverses the meaning. (c) swaps は for で, which doesn't fit here.

contrast_examples.en: The eyes are looking for someone.
(same subject marked with が — presentational, less natural here)
